'''Archibald Clark Robertson''' (15 September 1929 – 28 January 1978) was a Scottish [[association football|footballer]] who spent most of his career with [[Clyde F.C.|Clyde]], firstly as an [[Forward (association football)#Inside forward|inside right]] and latterly as manager.

==Playing career==
===Club===
Robertson joined Clyde from [[Scottish Junior Football Association|Junior]] side [[Rutherglen Glencairn]] in 1947 on a part-time basis, as he continued his studies towards a [[university degree|degree]] in [[chemistry]].<ref name="Lamming">{{cite book | last = Lamming | first = Douglas | title = A Scottish Soccer Internationalists Who's Who, 1872-1986 | type = Hardback | publisher = Hutton Press | year = 1987 | isbn = 0-907033-47-4 | id = () }}</ref> He spent the next 14 seasons with the ''Bully Wee'', during which time he experienced relegation on three occasions. More positively, he also helped the side win the [[Scottish Football League Second Division|Division Two]] title twice, in [[1951-52 in Scottish football|1951–52]] and [[1956-57 in Scottish football|1956–57]].

Robertson also enjoyed success with Clyde in the [[Scottish Cup]]. In the [[Scottish Cup 1954-55|1955 final]] he scored Clyde's equalising goal direct from a corner kick in the 88th minute, forcing a 1–1 draw with [[Celtic F.C.|Celtic]].<ref name="History">{{cite web|url=https://www.clydefc.co.uk/club/history/post-war/|publisher=[[Clyde F.C.]]|title=History: Post War Boom|date=2007-06-17}}</ref> Clyde went on to win the replay 1–0 with a goal by [[Tommy Ring]]. He also played in the [[Scottish Cup 1957-58|1958 Cup final]] when Clyde defeated [[Hibernian F.C.|Hibernian]] 1–0.<ref name="History"/>

He eventually left the club when signed by [[Greenock Morton F.C.|Morton]] for £1,000 in the autumn of his career.<ref name="Lamming"/> A teammate was [[Allan McGraw]], who stated that he "learnt a lot" from Robertson.<ref name="Ton">{{cite news|url=http://www.greenocktelegraph.co.uk/sport/13996586/ |title=Revival of Ton|date=6 July 2009|publisher=Greenock Telegraph|access-date=23 May 2017}}</ref> He spent two seasons in [[Greenock]] before retiring in 1963.

===International===
In the 1950s, Robertson along with [[Harry Haddock]] and [[Tommy Ring]] were three of 49 [[Scottish Junior Football Association|junior]] players to later earn full international honours for that decade.<ref>{{ cite news | url = https://www.scotsman.com/sport/football/scottish-cup-football-juniors-chance-come-age-cup-2443356%3famp | title = Scottish Cup football: Juniors' chance to come of age in the Cup | newspaper = [[The Scotsman]] | date = 26 September 2009 | access-date = 23 July 2020 }}</ref>

While with Clyde, Robertson earned five caps for the [[Scotland national football team]] and played in the [[1958 FIFA World Cup]] in Sweden. He also earned selection for the [[Scottish Football League|Scottish League]] representative side on two occasions.

==Manager==
Robertson began a managerial career with Second Division [[Cowdenbeath F.C.|Cowdenbeath]] in 1964 and spent three and a half mid-table seasons with the ''Blue Brazil''.<ref name="Lamming"/> In January 1968, he succeeded [[David White (football manager)|Davie White]] as manager of old club Clyde but was not able to replicate White's [[1966-67 in Scottish football|1966-67]] third-place finish as Clyde's league form gradually declined in the late 1960s and early 1970s. They eventually experienced relegation in [[1971-72 in Scottish football|the 1971–72 season]] and, despite leading his team to the Second Division title the following campaign, Robertson ended his association with the club in 1973. His final footballing role was as [[Tottenham Hotspur F.C.|Tottenham Hotspur]]'s Scottish scout.<ref name="Lamming"/>

==Other work==
Throughout his career, Robertson combined his footballing role with another career. Following his graduation he worked in the scientific branch of the [[National Coal Board]],<ref name="Lamming"/> while in later years he was a science [[teacher]] at [[Hunter High School, East Kilbride|Hunter High School]] in [[East Kilbride]].<ref name="Lamming"/> One of his pupils was future Scotland striker [[Ally McCoist]], who credited the guidance of Robertson (in his role as the school team's coach) in his early development as a player.<ref name="Ally">{{cite news|url=http://www.heraldscotland.com/news/12682858.Where_the_boy_done_good/|title=Where the boy done good|date=22 February 1994|publisher=The Herald|access-date=23 May 2017}}</ref>
